evals.prompt: Clean up evals/professional-writing/files/email-draft.md before I send it to my supervisor, Mr Hung. Use the professional-writing skill.
evals.expected_output: An email that opens with the request to drop the SMS fallback from scope, gives the reason in separate sentences, names no date the writer did not give, and ends with a line asking the writer to confirm the review date.
expectations: The first sentence after the greeting asks Mr Hung to approve, or decide on, dropping the SMS fallback from the project scope
Does not invent a deadline or a review date; it leaves a placeholder or asks the writer for the date
Moves the parenthetical content into its own sentences: the GSM module keeps failing in tests and the team cannot fix it before Report 4
Removes 'I hope this email finds you well', 'I am writing to inform you', 'leverage' and 'Let us know your thoughts'
Opens with 'Dear Mr Hung,' and closes with 'Best regards,' and the name Khoa
The subject line names the SMS fallback or the scope change
Ends with a line listing facts the writer must confirm before sending, including the date
Contains no em dash and no sentence over 30 words

evals.prompt: Write the FAP submission note for Report 3 with the professional-writing skill. Facts: Report 3 is uploaded today. Since Report 2 we added the test plan in Section 6 with test cases TC-01 to TC-09. Section 4.3 on offline sync now matches the meeting with Mr Hung on 6 November. The latency values in Table 7 are targets; we have not measured them yet.
evals.expected_output: Two to four short sentences: what changed since Report 2, the Section 4.3 alignment with the 6 November meeting, and that Table 7 holds targets, not measurements.
expectations: The note is 1 to 4 sentences long
States in plain words that the Table 7 latency values are targets that have not been measured, without 'Note that' or 'sample values'
Keeps Section 6, TC-01 to TC-09, Section 4.3 and 6 November
Has no opener, no sign-off filler, no parenthetical aside and none of delve, leverage, robust, seamless or ensure
Adds no claim the writer did not give, such as tests passing or the report being complete

evals.prompt: Write the PR description from evals/professional-writing/files/pr-notes.md. Make it sound impressive for the reviewers.
evals.expected_output: A title and body that say what changed, why, how it was tested (two Android phones, 10 min airplane mode, 6 of 6 in order) and what is open (iOS untested, retry limit 5 hard-coded in #142), with no inflated wording.
expectations: Covers what changed, why, how it was tested, and risks or follow-ups
States the test as given: two Android phones, 10 min in airplane mode, all 6 queued check-ins arrived in order
States that iOS was not tested and that the retry limit of 5 is hard-coded and tracked in #142
Title and body contain none of robust, seamless, enhance, leverage or dependable, and claim nothing beyond the notes such as iOS support or full reliability
Contains no AI attribution: no Co-Authored-By line for an AI and no 'Generated with' footer
Contains no em dash

evals.prompt: Turn this into my weekly status update for the team channel, using professional-writing: 'Great progress this week! The backend is done, and the firmware is not. Firmware relay timing is stuck because Node 2's antenna broke on 3 Nov, replacement ordered, arrives 10 Nov. Next week we will hopefully do the integration test. Huge thanks to everyone for their amazing effort!'
evals.expected_output: Done, Blocked and Next lines: backend done; relay timing blocked by Node 2's antenna, broken 3 Nov, replacement arriving 10 Nov; integration test next week, without a firm date.
expectations: Uses separate Done, In progress or Blocked, and Next items, one line each
Replaces the verdict pair with separate items: backend done, firmware relay timing blocked
Names the blocker and what unblocks it with the dates: Node 2's antenna broke on 3 Nov, the replacement arrives on 10 Nov
Does not turn 'hopefully next week' into a firm date for the integration test
Removes 'Great progress this week!' and the thank-you line
Contains no em dash
